decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach; live key is farther forward and slightly left of reference. Keep left parked.
Continue smooth right approach with raised elbow, rotating the fingers downward above the key.
Advance above the key while maintaining continuous elbow-up posture; next refine yaw and lateral alignment from wrist view.
Align downward gripper with live key's angled shaft and move above its grasp point; keep open during approach.
Wrist view shows shaft left of grasp center and still angled. Correct leftward, descend slightly, and match its yaw before closing.
Fine-align shaft over the pinch point, correct slight yaw overshoot, and begin closing around the shaft near its bow.
Center the lower shaft between the closing fingers and fully close. Retention will be checked with a short vertical lift.
Lift the pinched key vertically by about 7 cm, keeping the right gripper fully closed and watching for retention.
Key remains in the right fingers after lifting. Raise and rotate it toward the central handover while beginning the left arm's elbow-up approach.
Continue rotating the retained key for handover while raising and advancing the receiving left gripper without crossing arms.
Bring both hands toward the central handover region, keeping the key horizontal and the left fingers open with elbow-up continuity.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller left-arm increments after the continuity guard; maintain the right-hand grip during handover positioning.
Settle the right hand into a horizontal-key handover pose and orient the left fingers to receive the bow.
Advance the left receiver toward the visible bow, holding the right hand fixed. Partly narrow the receiver only after reaching the approach pose.
Approach the key bow with the partly open left fingers; keep the right grip closed until the receiver surrounds the bow.
Wrist view places the bow below the receiver's center. Lower the left hand slightly, advance the last centimeter, and gently narrow around the bow.
The bow is contacting the receiving fingers. Make a small centering correction and close the left gripper fully while retaining the right support.
Bow appears seated between the left fingers. Hold that grip closed and gradually release the right hand for transfer.
Key moved out of the receiving pinch after release; transfer is not secure. Separate the open hands and reassess its settled location for recovery.
Key has fallen onto the table in the right workspace. Withdraw the receiver and reorient the right gripper for a new pickup.
Continue downward approach and yaw alignment to the fallen key, keeping the left hand safely withdrawn.
Descend toward the lower shaft while continuing yaw alignment; key remains visible on the table.
Complete shaft yaw alignment and bring the open right fingers near table grasp height, correcting their small downward-axis tilt.
Center the aligned shaft in the right pinch point and lower to pickup height, leaving the bow exposed for a clearer second handover.
The shaft now crosses the pinch center with the bow exposed. Correct its slight angle and close the right gripper for recovery.
The closing fingers nudged the key slightly off center. Recenter the lower shaft with a brief partial opening, then close again.
Let the right fingers finish closing without lateral motion, then test retention with a short vertical lift.
Continue the vertical retention test with the right gripper closed; verify that the key follows rather than remaining on the table.
The key is retained but has pivoted at the tooth-side grip. Raise it clear of the table and rotate toward a new bow handover, checking its actual hanging pose.
The key slipped from the tooth grip. Approach its new table position with the fingers open, aiming farther down the bare shaft rather than the teeth.
Descend with the open fingers, bringing the bare shaft toward the grasp center and correcting its leftward image offset.
Lower cautiously and shift toward the bow so the pinch is on the bare shaft rather than the teeth; keep open until aligned.
Tracking suggests table contact, so stop descending, lift slightly, and correct the shaft's image position with the fingers open.
Use the head view to bring the fingertips back over the visible bare shaft; maintain height to avoid further table contact.
Close around the centered bare shaft, with a small backward correction so the teeth remain clear of the pinch.
Finish closing on the bare shaft without lateral motion, then make a small vertical retention test.
The key is tilting against the tooth-side contact. Reopen over the table and move the pinch farther toward the bow for a bare-shaft grasp.
The bare shaft is now clear of the teeth at the pinch height. Align its slight tilt and center it while closing.
Hold still while the fingers finish closing near the bow, then test this grasp with a small lift.
The bow follows the fingers in the short test. Lift vertically with the grasp fully closed before attempting another handover.
The key is stably lifted in the bow grasp. Raise and rotate gradually toward the receiving hand while keeping the left hand clear.
Maintain the stable bow grip while raising and yawing toward handover; bring the open receiver closer but outside contact.
Continue the slow supported rotation and raise the bow toward receiver height; keep the receiver open and clear.
Finish positioning the raised key for handover and approach its bow with the open left receiver, using small continuous motions.
Advance the receiver toward the bow visible in the right wrist view and lower slightly to center it vertically, retaining right-hand support.
The bow is centered between the receiving fingers. Advance one final centimeter and close the left gripper while maintaining right support.
Keep the receiver closed on the bow and slowly unload the right grip, checking whether the key remains seated in the left fingers.
The key stays centered in the left pinch as the right opens. Fully release and withdraw the right hand to verify the handover.
Key remains seated in the left hand. Withdraw the right hand and begin a continuous elbow-up rotation of the key toward upright insertion.
Continue the left-hand pose adjustment along a smooth raised arc; park the released right hand outside the insertion area.
Replan from the executed prefix with reduced rotation increments after the joint-continuity guard. Keep the transferred key closed in the left hand.
Carry the retained key leftward toward the live lock while rotating toward vertical insertion with small continuous increments.
Continue the raised leftward arc and upright rotation; key remains seated in the left fingers and the right arm stays clear.
Finish bringing the key upright above the live lock; maintain clearance before fine slot alignment.
Match the key plane to the visible slot angle and make a small lateral/downward alignment correction above the lock.
Fine-center the visible slot under the key and remove its remaining small angular mismatch, descending only 5 mm.
Slot appears centered behind the shaft. Lower the upright key 15 mm in small steps, holding its yaw and grip fixed.
The tip remains visible beyond the slot rather than occluding into it. Relieve slightly upward and make a small in-plane correction toward the hole.
Refine the remaining tip-to-slot in-plane offset without additional downward motion; keep the key upright and retained.
The tip now overlaps the slot opening. Attempt a slow straight insertion while preserving the upright pose and closed left grip.
Continue the aligned vertical insertion another 2 cm in small increments, watching for key movement or contact-induced deflection.
